newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Kosovo trial was flawed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Kosovo trial was flawed.

text.p: A trial at which 20 ethnic Albanians were jailed for alleged terrorism in Serbia's troubled Kosovo province last week was marked by "serious irregularities", the United States said on Monday.
The group, whose members received a total of 107 years in prison last Friday, was charged with association for the purpose of hostile activity, threatening territorial integrity, and terrorism.

"While the United States government is deeply concerned by acts of terrorism that have plagued Kosovo in recent months, the defendants' trial was marred by a number of serious judicial irregularities," the State Department said.
Spokesman John Dinger said the conduct of the trial failed to meet contemporary judicial standards, "including those supposedly enforced under the Serbian constitution".

Evidence was not controlled, defendants were frequently denied access to their attorneys during the case, and the judge refused to allow a number of relevant interventions by the defence to be entered into the official court record, Dinger said.
U.S. embassy officials and other international observers attended the proceedings.

Avni Klinaku, the prime defendant, was sentenced to 10 years in prison. He admitted being a member of a clandestine organisation, the National Movement for the Liberation of Kosovo, but denied involvement in terrorism.
Kosovo, where ethnic Albanians outnumber Serbs nine to one, is widely regarded as a political powder keg which, if ignited, could wreck international peace efforts in the Balkans.

Some 30 people, both Serbs and Albanians, have been killed over the past year in guerrilla violence. Serbian police cracked down on the province in January, arresting some 70 people in a sweep following the guerrilla attacks.
The United States has made an improvement in Serbia's treatment of Kosovo one of its conditions for lifting remaining sanctions in force against rump Yugoslavia -- Serbia and Montenegro.
